title: QBR: VelaStream Inference Health & Cost Sync
summary: Quarterly health review focused on usage trends, rising token costs, latency regressions on tail traffic, Dedicated capacity evaluation, and alignment on roadmap priorities. Agreed pilot benchmarks, security doc share, and follow-up pricing model options.
topics: next quarter roadmap and cutover timeline
action_items: Maya Chen | Send VelaStream tailored pilot pricing grid and 6-week SOW draft | 2027-09-10
Oliver Grant | Run 95th percentile latency perf test with current prompt set, share traces | 2027-09-14
Priya Rao | Provide sample peak-window traffic CSV and list of 5 critical prompts | 2027-09-09
Rina Patel | Share SOC2 + architecture diagram + KMS integration notes | 2027-09-11
next_steps: SE to run perf tests and report p95/p99 over 72 hour window
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-09-07 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen, Oliver Grant, Rina Patel (Redwood); Priya Rao, Derek Mills, Sofia Alvarez, Tom Ngyuen (VelaStream)

Summary: Quick QBR to map cost/usage trends and triage a recent latency tail. VelaStream is seeing a 28% token burn increase month-over-month driven by a new conversational feature; cost pressure from high p95 latency causing more retries. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted, security checklist, and concrete next steps for a short pilot.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining i think we've got a packed agenda so we'll try to keep to time, quick intros?
[00:06] Priya Rao: hi this is priya, head of ml ops at velastream, i'll kick us off from our side, thanks for the invite
[00:10] Derek Mills: Derek here vp eng, i'll be listening in on infra and cost implications
[00:14] Sofia Alvarez: Sofia sres, focused on latency and incident history
[00:18] Tom Ngyuen: Tom, finops, hi all
[00:21] Maya Chen: perfect, maya from redwood, with oliver our se and rina csm
[00:25] Oliver Grant: hey all

[00:40] Maya Chen: ok quick context - priya sent us the usage spike data, feel free to correct me: about 28% month over month token increase, most from the new convo flow, and you're seeing more client retries at peak; that's driving costs up and p95 tail on some routes is spiking to 1.8s, correct?
[00:55] Priya Rao: yep that's right; our p50 is fine around 250-300ms but the tail is what bites us during spikes and the retries are, well they're killing the margins. also curious about caching and batching settings, we haven't tuned them much.
[01:10] Maya Chen: makes sense. before we dig in, can you describe where you're hosted? cloud region, VPC, any dedicated infra?
[01:18] Derek Mills: we're multi-region on GCP, VPC peering to redwood currently using hosted api. no dedicated capacity yet, we looked at dedicated but wanted to validate traffic patterns first.
[01:28] Oliver Grant: ok, that helps. a couple of quick calls outs: prefix caching can shave repeated prompt prefixes, and the runtime supports automatic KV cache reuse; we sometimes see folks misconfigure windowing and lose cache hits, which makes tail tokens more expensive.
[01:45] Sofia Alvarez: can you explain prefix cache a bit in lay terms? is it something our app needs to implement?
[01:50] Oliver Grant: short answer: minimal app changes. you can set a cache key based on user conversation ids and we keep the KV cache across calls. for the hosted api we do it automatically if the request includes session_id; for private/dedicated you can keep the cache in the same runtime with sticky routing. sometimes the SDK doesn't set session_id consistently so hits are lost.
[02:10] Priya Rao: we do set session ids but i think there are some older services still using the older client library.

[02:25] Maya Chen: on the latency regressions — we ran a quick runbook on our side, and a common pattern is mixing long-context prompts with short prompts in the same pool, that forces kernels to recompile or shift memory patterns causing p95 jitter. Oliver can explain technical detail.
[02:40] Oliver Grant: yeah basically the scheduler picks kernels based on observed seq length; very spiky distributions cause less efficient batching. the runtime has a quantization friendly path but if models are switching configs you get stalls. also there was a small KV cache evict bug in a older runtime we rolled a patch for last month, but i want to test against your exact prompt set.
[03:05] Derek Mills: that KV bug — are we likely to have hit it? our spike started late july.
[03:11] Oliver Grant: possibly if you were on that older runtime; rina will follow up with the runtime version used. we can run a targeted trace.

[03:25] Sofia Alvarez: security question: we have to route audit logs to our SIEM and tie keys to our KMS. how mature is the hosted integration for external KMS and per-request encryption?
[03:36] Rina Patel: we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (GCP KMS, AWS KMS) for Private deployments today; for Hosted we have envelope encryption with an option for bring-your-own-key via partner integrations — i'll share the current doc. audit logs: we provide per-request logs and long-term retention as an add-on.
[03:56] Tom Ngyuen: is SSO/SAML enterprise-ready? we need SCIM provisioning and RBAC controls in the console.
[04:04] Maya Chen: yes SAML SSO + SCIM + RBAC exists; we also have token scoping and route-level permissions for enterprise tiers. we'll include the security deck.

[04:18] Priya Rao: back to costs — Tom's concerned about per-token burn on short-turnaround calls; is there a path to reduce unit cost without losing quality? quantization? smaller model variants?
[04:30] Oliver Grant: tradeoffs: a quantized model can reduce GPU time and cost but may slightly change output distribution; we can recommend a fallback routing policy: route low-risk inference to a quantized variant and high-critical routes to FP16. Also batching tweaks and cache will reduce unit tokens. Redwood Optimize can give suggestions programmatically after a 72-hour trace.
[04:50] Maya Chen: conceptually we suggest 3 levers: 1) caching & batching tuning, 2) selective quantization and model variants, 3) routing policies for peak vs steady. We can show a projected cost delta once we have your traffic sample.

[05:05] Derek Mills: what about Dedicated? if we reserve a pool do we actually lower p95 and unit cost reliably? our finance team prefers reserved commits if the math works.
[05:16] Oliver Grant: Dedicated gives a more predictable kernel placement and you avoid noisy neighbor effects; also autoscale and burst capacity configs let you buy headroom. Pricing is usually reserved monthly commit plus usage; there is an inflection point where it pays vs hosted, depends on steady-state QPS and peak shape.
[05:34] Priya Rao: curious what the inflection looks like — are there example benchmarks?
[05:38] Maya Chen: yes, we'll provide a comparative spreadsheet: estimate cost/100k queries for hosted vs 2-tier dedicated setups. that's part of the action item for maya.

[05:50] Sofia Alvarez: on reliability — we had two incidents in august; one was a region failover, the other was a repeat input that caused a runaway KV state. any mitigations?
[05:59] Oliver Grant: for region failover we recommend cross-region routing policies and auto-fallback to compatible model variants; for KV runaway we can set upper bounds on cache size per session and eviction strategies. also we can instrument alerting hooks to your pager so SREs see token anomalies.

[06:20] Priya Rao: what's the timeline for the pilot you mentioned? we'd like to scope a six-week pilot to validate perf and cost improvements.
[06:27] Rina Patel: six weeks is doable. typical cadence: week 0 onboarding & baseline trace, week 1-2 tuning, week 3 perf run, week 4 scale tests, week 5-6 wrap up and final cost model.
[06:40] Tom Ngyuen: ok would finance sign a small commitment for that? we need clear acceptance criteria.
[06:45] Maya Chen: acceptance criteria proposal: 15% p95 reduction OR 20% unit cost savings for the targeted routes, with no regression on latency-sensitive routes. we'll put this in the SOW.

[07:00] Derek Mills: regarding data residency — some of our customers require EU-only processing, are there region pinning controls?
[07:07] Maya Chen: yes region pinning and routing by policy available; for Private we can deploy into your EU VPC, or for Hosted we can pin traffic to our EU region and provide compliance docs.

[07:20] Priya Rao: one more technical — our prompt set mixes long context (8k) with short followups, could we get a recommendation on model selection?
[07:28] Oliver Grant: recommend splitting: long-context model for the initial generation and a short-seq fast model for followups, using cached KV to avoid recomputation. Another approach is model rollouts with canaries for 10% traffic to validate quality.

[07:46] Maya Chen: ok we'll outline a concrete phased approach: 1) collect traces and critical prompts, 2) run reproducible p95 tests on your dataset, 3) implement cache + batching changes, 4) evaluate quantized variants, 5) finalize SOW for Dedicated pilot if needed.

[08:05] Priya Rao: sounds good. can you also include a risks page — what could cause the pilot to not hit targets?
[08:12] Rina Patel: yes we'll do a risk matrix: noisy sequences, incomplete session ids, uninstrumented clients, and model output drift.

[08:25] Tom Ngyuen: i want to make sure finance can see the delta per token and per-month; show both raw hosted rate and committed-dedicated amortized cost.
[08:34] Maya Chen: noted — we'll send the cost model and an example amortization across a 12-month commit.

[08:45] Derek Mills: any regulatory items — do you support detailed audit logs for per-request data access? we need retention to 1 year for some customers.
[08:54] Rina Patel: yes audit logs available as an add-on, we can export to your SIEM and define retention; for Private deployments you control retention fully.

[09:05] Sofia Alvarez: small note on our side — some clients are on an old SDK that doesn't propagate session ids, we'll put together a list of services to upgrade.
[09:12] Priya Rao: agreed we'll give you that list.

[09:20] Maya Chen: great. Oliver can you talk about the perf test plan you'll run?
[09:24] Oliver Grant: i'll take your prompt set and run a 72-hour perf window with p50/p95/p99, trace key request paths, and surface hot kernels; i'll also run a synthetic peak using your peak-window csv to simulate bursts. expect a first pass report in 6 business days.
[09:40] Derek Mills: do you need whitelisted ip ranges for the load gen?
[09:43] Oliver Grant: yes we'll need ephemeral keys and potentially CIDR allowlist; rina and priya can coordinate.

[09:55] Maya Chen: we should talk about rollout strategy if pilot hits targets — gradual canary then shift traffic via routing policy.
[10:00] Priya Rao: timeline question: if pilot succeeds, how quickly can we cut over to Dedicated?
[10:05] Oliver Grant: provisioning a Dedicated pool is typically 2-4 weeks depending on region and sizing; there is a small lead time for capacity and network setup.

[10:20] Tom Ngyuen: any long lived costs for observability? we want token-level analytics and per-route latency dashboards.
[10:26] Rina Patel: those are part of Redwood Console; we have a free tier but token-level retention beyond 90 days is an add-on. we'll include options in the pricing grid.

[10:40] Priya Rao: ok are there any gotchas around model variant compatibility when switching? e.g. rollbacks and output parity?
[10:48] Oliver Grant: small differences expected between quantized and fp16 variants; we recommend a quality monitor tied to prompt tests and automatic rollback on regressions. Redwood Optimize can auto-suggest thresholds.

[11:05] Maya Chen: time check — we have about 40 minutes left, good progress. let's do a quick recap and confirm action owners.
[11:12] Rina Patel: recap: maya sends pricing + SOW draft; oliver runs perf and shares traces; priya supplies traffic csv and prompt list; rina shares security and SOC2 docs.
[11:22] Priya Rao: yes that's right

[11:30] Derek Mills: i'm comfortable moving to a small pilot commitment once we see the SOW and cost math.
[11:35] Tom Ngyuen: finance will review the amortized committed numbers and give a thumbs up if it's favorable.

[11:45] Maya Chen: super. any final questions?
[11:48] Sofia Alvarez: maybe one — can we get an emergency rollback playbook in the pilot? fast fail plan.
[11:53] Oliver Grant: yes we'll include a rollback playbook and signal thresholds to auto-revert.

[12:05] Maya Chen: great thanks everyone, we'll shoot the pricing and docs by end of week, and oliver will start the perf test once we get the sample prompts.
[12:12] Priya Rao: thank you, appreciate the clarity, talk soon
[12:15] Derek Mills: thanks all
[12:17] Meeting ended
